To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the joint effect of the HLA-DR, INS and PTCN22 genes on T1D risk is higher in the family data set compared to the case-control one, that the risk conferred by the three genes together increases with the age at disease onset and that the risk conferred is higher in the case-control data set for the high risk HLA-DB1 genotype category, compared to the family data set.
the joint risk of T1D conferred by HLA, INS-VNTRA and PTPN2 genes is higher than the sum of their single risk.

the joint risk of HLA,INS and PTPN2 genes is higher than the sum of the individual risks of each gene, and that the risk of carrying a combination of high, moderate and low risk HLA alleles with at risk INS or PTPN22 alleles is 11.5, 1.7 and 0.2%, respectively, in the case-control data set and 19.9, 6.6 and 2.1%, respectively, in a French
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of T1D genetic susceptibility and the development of a new approach for the identification of individuals at increased risk of developing T1D.
the assessment of the risk conferred by these three genes on the onset and development of T1D.
the development of new statistical methods to study the joint effect of several genes and to identify the genetic risk factors in a population-based case-control study and in a family data set.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the joint risk of HLA, PTPN22 and INS genes in T1D is not negligible.
the HLA locus is the major susceptibility gene for T1D, and the INS and PTPNA2 genes are only marginally involved in T1D susceptibility, especially for patients with low risk HLA genotypes.

, in a Caucasian population with a broad range of age at onset, HLA, INS-VN TR and PTPN 22 genes confer a cumulative risk of 1:10 in the case-control and a cumulative risk of approximately 1:5 in the family cohort.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the joint effect of all three susceptibility loci increases the T1D risk by a factor of 2-3, depending on the data set.
the BN model provides an effective tool for assessing genetic risk in T1D.
, the BN probabilistic model is a suitable approach to estimate genetic risk in T1D and to assess the joint effect of multiple genetic loci.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Bayesian Network approach can be applied to the study of complex diseases, in particular in the context of genetic susceptibility, and that it is able to provide a more accurate estimation of risk conferred by the joint effect of several genes.
the BN approach can be used to assess joint risk conferred by several genetic susceptibility loci in both case-control and population-based family data sets.
the joint analysis of these three genes is a promising strategy for the assessment of T1D genetic risk, especially in young children.
